*   *In-scattering:* Light from other directions reflected into the view ray.
*   *Out-scattering:* Light from the view ray reflected away.
*   **Rayleigh Scattering:** Used when $r \ll \lambda$ (e.g., smoke, dust, water molecules).
*   **Mie Scattering:** Used when $r \approx \lambda$ (e.g., fog, water droplets).
The method was developed to address the high variance and computational cost of direct path tracing in highly scattering media, where many bounces are required to capture indirect illumination.
These methods are widely used in offline rendering and high-quality visual effects where accurate simulation of light transport in fog, smoke, and translucent materials is critical.
